newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofgas and Offer to merge by 2000 - Spottiswoode.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofgas and Offer to merge by 2000 - Spottiswoode.

text.p: The UK's gas and electricity regulators, Ofgas and Offer, should be merged by the end of the century, Ofgas Director General Clare Spottiswoode said on Wednesday.

Answering questions at an industry conference, Spottiswoode said that as soon as existing committments allow, Dr Eileen Marshall, Ofgas Director of Regulation and business affairs will start spending one day a week at Offer.
"By 2000 the two should be merged", she said. "This winter will see a lot more interaction (betwen Offer and Ofgas) than ever before. Eventually they will be merged".
Spottiswoode said she was "very pleased" with the performance of the UK gas industry since the second phase or "hard landing" of the Network Code was introduced on September 1.
"It's gone remarkably smoothly and we're very pleased", she said. "That's not to say that we're not worried about this winter - we are.

"There are lots of opportunities for people to make clerical errors, and we've seen some of those. And there are lots of opportunities for people to make commercial errors. So we are not relaxed, but we are pleased".
